references.text: Jesus meets the outcast man and reveals his messianic identity, leading the man to believe and worship him, in contrast to those who cast him out.
The first time the Pharisees threaten excommunication (expulsion from the synagogue) for anyone who confesses Jesus as the Messiah, which happens directly in this verse.
The blind man's logical counterargument to the Pharisees: that God does not hear sinners, but listens to those who fear him and do his will.
A previous conflict in the same chapter where the Pharisees are divided and ask whether Jesus is a sinner, setting up the final conclusion in verse 34.
Jesus comments on the judgment of those who refuse to see, claiming that their sin remains, confirming the Pharisees' own condition in verse 34.
Describes how many believed in Jesus but did not confess it for fear of being expelled from the synagogue, a direct consequence of the threat in verse 34.
Jesus predicts that those who kill his disciples will think they are offering service to God, just as the Pharisees in verse 34 thought they were defending God's honor.
